title: Jellyfish and sea creature stings | NHS inform
text:
Jellyfish and sea creature stings
In Scotland, there are some sea creatures that can bite or sting. This includes:
jellyfish
sea urchins
weever fish
Portuguese man-of-war
Most stings in Scotland are mild and can be easily treated.
Symptoms of sea creature stings
The main symptoms of sea creature stings are intense pain where you were stung and an itchy rash.
Jellyfish and Portuguese man-of-war stings can also cause raised stripes on the skin (welts).
Go to A&E or phone 999 if:
You or someone else has been stung by a sea creature and have:
difficulty breathing
chest pain
fits or seizures
severe swelling around the affected area
severe bleeding
vomiting
light-headedness
loss of consciousness
Phone 111 if:
You have been stung by a sea creature:
on your mouth, throat or near your eyes
and have severe pain that’s not going away
in a tropical country
while travelling outside the UK and have a high temperature or a wound that does not get better
You should also get help if you’ve been stung by a stingray.
What to do if you’ve been stung by a sea creature
If you’ve been stung by a sea creature, you should ask a lifeguard or someone with first aid training for help.
If help is not available, you should:
Rinse the affected area with sea water (not fresh water).
Remove any spines or stings with tweezers. Do not use your fingers to remove them.
Soak the area in warm water (as warm as you can tolerate).
Take painkillers like
paracetamol
or
ibuprofen
to manage pain.
You should not use an ice pack on the wound or press the area.
How to prevent sea creature bites and stings
If you’re swimming or paddling outdoors, there are some things you can do to help prevent stings.
Do
wear a wetsuit and rash vest
wear waterproof shoes
look out for warning signs for sea creatures on beaches
stamp your feet in shallow water – so that sea creatures know something is approaching
Get more advice on how to swim safely in Scotland’s outdoor water
Images of sea creatures
Moon jellyfish
Moon jellyfish are common in the UK and often float just below the water’s surface.
Moon jellyfish on beach
It’s common for jellyfish to wash up on beaches. Watch out for them if you’re walking or playing on the beach.
Sea urchins
Sea urchins are found around the UK’s shores.
Weever fish
Weever fish live buried in the sand but can sting if they’re disturbed.
Portuguese man-of-war
Portuguese man-of-war float on the surface of the water and have a bad sting.
